pitch_detail.notes: Starts up the bolted line of The Struggle Within, climbing a crack past its first four bolts, then steps right to the belay bolts beneath the second pitch of the East Wall route.
Bolted climbing that trends up and right to reach the arete followed by Eye of the Beholder. Pitches 1 and 2 can be linked on a 70 m rope if the rope is managed with long runners.
Easy natural-gear climbing at about 5.7 leads to one bolt-protected hard move, then a crack that widens up to a hanging belay. Pitches 3 and 4 can be linked on a 70 m rope with runners.
A wide crack taking 4-inch gear, then the line veers right to a bolted finish over a bulge. Belay on a ledge.
Easy bolted face climbing on imperfect rock up to an anchor. Pitches 5 and 6 can be linked on a 70 m rope.
A bolted face crosses a section of poor rock; the holds near the top are solid.

The best climbing of the route, on good rock high on the finishing tower. At the arete, clip a bolt for the follower and step down around the edge to a ledge. The anchor here is not meant for rappelling.
Step right to a bolted water streak and stem past dubious rock to a better finish. Belay from the slings or bolts just over the lip, or continue to the summit and belay there.

review.changed: Wrote 8 pitch notes from the single route page (grades, bolt counts, linking advice). No pitch lengths stated, so none given. No rappel_detail: sources give no station-by-station descent and report that anchors were once pulled then later said present but hard to find.
review.other_findings: Stored descent says seven rappels with a 70 m rope; not confirmed by the source read. Page says anchors on the rappel route had been removed (2014), later said to exist but hard to find. Pitch 8 has no stated grade. Pitch text on the source page is credited to a guidebook, so only one independent source.

pitch_detail.notes: Begin at the double-crack left of the large flake. Climb right of two thin cracks until they split, take the left fork to cruxy face moves past a single bolt, then easier face climbing to the two-bolt belay.
Step left onto an exposed arete, then climb right past a short parallel crack system. Continue up the obvious flake system and finish to the right where the flake ends.

review.changed: Only pitches 1 and 2 were available, via search-result excerpts (direct fetch of both pages was blocked). P1 120 ft converted to 37 m. No rappel_detail written: excerpts say a free-air rappel off the north side with two ropes, while the stored descent says westward to a saddle; sources conflict and no station detail was read.
review.other_findings: Mountain Project lists 6 pitches / 700 ft; stored row says 5 pitches. Stored descent (rappel westward to saddle) disagrees with the north-side free-air rappel in the excerpt.
